pairs.question: Nonne vestes tuae viliores sunt corpore tuo?
pairs.derivation: In Dromodotus's Socratic chain he asks a genuine nonne-interrogative; Crobolus genuinely affirms with 'Sunt' (they are). Dropped the framing 'Unico tecum agam argumento, Socratico more. Quid censes?' which narrates/leads into the asking. Answer window ends at 'Sunt' (first full stop); the following 'Sed quid inde?' turns from answering to a new query, so it is cut.

pairs.question: Nonne, quod est melius, id est nobilius?
pairs.derivation: Dromodotus asks a genuine nonne-interrogative; Crobolus genuinely concedes with 'Do id tibi' (I grant you that). Speaker labels stripped; whole reply is the affirming answer.

pairs.question: Et animi bona meliora quam corporis?
pairs.derivation: Dromodotus asks an elliptical interrogative (Et animi bona meliora quam corporis? = 'And the goods of the soul [are] better than [those] of the body?'); Crobolus genuinely affirms with 'Proculdubio' (Undoubtedly). Speaker labels stripped; the other nonne-questions in this chain (e.g. 'Nonne corpus tuum praestantius est vestibus?') are dropped because they get non-answering deflections (Idem per idem, Quorsum haec, Progredere, Conclude), not real answers.
